clue.text: A quick haircut outside university hall

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one thing standing outside another wraps around it, so the haircut goes round the university

parts.note: a trim is a quick, light haircut
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student gets a speedy haircut just outside a university hall of residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hall' looks like part of the university scene, but it is the definition; U sits inside TRIM, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is the large open entrance hall or central court of a building.

clue.text: South African philosophy club untucked trousers

indicators.note: as a verb, to trouser is to pocket, so these words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, after the C and L and before the C, K, E and D

explanation.surface: A club of South African thinkers has a dress code problem: shirts hanging out of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' reads as a noun for clothing, but here it is a verb meaning pockets or holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubuntu is the Nguni Bantu ethic of shared humanity, a philosophy associated with Desmond Tutu and Nelson Mandela.

clue.text: Shakes from extremely stylish milk dispensers

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the two outside letters of stylish
udders are the organs that dispense a cow's milk

explanation.surface: Someone shakes a fancy milkshake out of very stylish dispensers.
explanation.definitionFit: To shudder is to tremble or shake convulsively, so shudders is a verb synonym of shakes.

clue.text: I don't believe that last gift's totally unwrapped

indicators.note: unwrapping strips the outer covering, and totally means both words lose their outside letters

parts.note: last without its first and last letters
gift without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone sceptical cannot believe the final present has been fully unwrapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'last' and 'gift' look like part of a Christmas morning, but each is a word to be peeled.
explanation.definitionFit: As if! is a scornful exclamation of disbelief, an idiom meaning that is hardly likely.

clue.text: At last, it's do or die — failing another way out

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the final letter of it's

indicators.note: something failing falls apart, so the phrase is broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A desperate escapee finds the do-or-die plan has failed and looks for an alternative exit.
explanation.definitionFit: A side door is a secondary entrance or exit, an alternative to the main way out of a building.

clue.text: Hunk and date aboard toboggan wrapped up warm

indicators.note: a passenger aboard is carried inside the vehicle, so these pieces sit within the sledge

parts.note: a sled is a toboggan or sledge
a wad is a thick lump or chunk
D is the abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A handsome man and his date ride a toboggan, bundled up against the cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hunk' wants to be an attractive man; here it is just a lump. A toboggan is a sledge, in American English a sled.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaddled describes being wound tightly in cloth or blankets, as a baby is kept snug and warm.

clue.text: Hans about to change his ways?

indicators.note: to change the order of letters is to rearrange them

parts.note: these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man called Hans is about to reform his behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His ways' looks like a person's habits; Hans is a typical German name, so his ways are German roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Autobahns are German motorways, the roads a German such as Hans would drive on.

clue.text: One's stoned, having foolish date on company time

parts.note: April 1st, April Fools' Day, written APR I
CO is the abbreviation for company
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs makes a silly date during working hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' suggests drugs, but it means having a stone, as fruit does.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a stone fruit, so it is one that has a stone in its middle.

clue.text: Moon having ghostly appearance gets one in a state

parts.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons
wan means pale and sickly, as a ghost looks

explanation.surface: A pale, spooky moon drives someone into a nervous state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' suggests agitation; it means living in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iowan is a resident of Iowa, one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: Calls from capsized sailor not getting an answer

indicators.note: a capsized boat is turned upside down, so the word is turned back to front
not getting something means going without it, so a letter is left out

parts.note: a seaman is a sailor
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Cries come from a sailor whose boat has overturned and who gets no reply.
explanation.walkthrough: Turn SEAMAN round to NAMAES, then drop its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To name someone is to call them something, so names is a verb synonym of calls.

clue.text: Sat on throne, dictator's not exactly hailed

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words for another to write down

parts.note: when it hails, ice falls rather than water, so it has not exactly done the wetter thing

explanation.surface: A despot is installed on the throne, but his reception is hardly a hero's welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' fits the throne picture as a tyrant, but signals speech: one who dictates says words aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To reign is to rule as monarch, which is pictured as sitting on the throne.

clue.text: Right rubbish home office decor

indicators.note: rubbish, read as a verb, means to trash or wreck, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone declares that the decoration of their home office is terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' sits like an exclamation of agreement, but it is the noun for an entitlement.
explanation.definitionFit: Freedom of choice is an entitlement to decide for oneself, often claimed as a basic human right.

clue.text: Part of network where one travelling to work needs other end of platform

indicators.note: needing the other end means one end of the word is traded for its opposite end

parts.note: a commuter travels to work each day
platform starts with this letter and ends with M; the commuter's second M is swapped for it

explanation.surface: A commuter needs to get to the far end of the station platform.
explanation.walkthrough: Platform runs from P to M, so in COMMUTER the M is replaced by the other end, P.
explanation.definitionFit: A computer is a node on a network, one of the machines linked together in it.

clue.text: Terms describing large spheres

indicators.note: to describe is also to draw around, so these words encircle the letter

parts.note: terms are words
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Some vocabulary describes big round objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' reads as explaining in words, but in geometry to describe a circle is to draw it round something.
explanation.definitionFit: Worlds and spheres are both used for planets or for fields of activity, as in the sporting sphere.

clue.text: One receiving hidden signals making inroads with traitors?

indicators.note: making suggests these letters are used to make something new by rearranging them

parts.note: these letters are reworked
these letters are reworked too

explanation.surface: A spy picking up secret messages is making progress against traitors.
explanation.walkthrough: The spy picture makes 'hidden signals' sound covert; they are just invisible radio waves.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor radio is a portable set that receives broadcast radio waves, which cannot be seen.

clue.text: US tax collectors slashing American rate for high-flying area

indicators.note: slashing cuts into something, so these letters are cut into the middle of the others

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
the IRS is the Internal Revenue Service, the US tax authority
pace is a rate of movement

explanation.surface: American tax officials cut the rate charged for a premium flight zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The IRS is the Internal Revenue Service; 'slashing' suggests cutting the price, but here it cuts into the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Airspace is the region of the sky above a country, where aircraft fly.

clue.text: Famous backing singers somehow mess up holding note

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so one piece is put within the other
somehow says the letters end up in some new, unspecified arrangement

parts.note: these letters are reworked
re is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Well-known backing vocalists manage to fluff a held note.
explanation.walkthrough: MESS UP is rearranged as SUPMES, and RE sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Supremes were the Motown group billed as Diana Ross and the Supremes, so they sang behind her.

clue.text: See 11
Poem about end of journey on ship taking years

definitions.text: Poem about end of journey on ship taking years

indicators.note: about means going around, so the poem's word wraps round the next pieces

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem
end of journey: its final letter
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
Y is the abbreviation for years

explanation.surface: A poem tells of the end of a voyage by ship that lasted years.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes Homer's poem, whose hero spends ten years sailing home from Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Odyssey is Homer's epic poem of Odysseus's long sea voyage home, taking a decade.

clue.text: Characters within cell revolutionised record number of countries

indicators.note: the characters within a word are its inner letters, with the outer ones dropped

parts.note: a nerve cell is a neuron; its inner letters are kept

indicators.note: a revolution turns something round, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Something inside a prison cell sparked a revolution that set a record.
explanation.walkthrough: The cell is a nerve cell, NEURON, not a prison cell.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is a continent made up of many countries, so it is a group of nations.

clue.text: Ruler from space periodically visited meteors

parts.note: an em is a printer's space

indicators.note: visiting periodically means calling at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: An alien ruler comes from outer space, regularly dropping in on meteors.
explanation.walkthrough: An em is a unit of spacing in typesetting.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, more often spelt emir, is a Muslim prince or ruler in the Middle East.

clue.text: A bit of drama ahead of Italian family's latest project

parts.note: Act IV, a fourth act, is one part of a play
IT is the abbreviation for Italian

indicators.note: the latest of something is the last one, here the final letter

parts.note: the last letter of family

explanation.surface: An Italian family's newest venture begins with a short theatrical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of drama' is not just ACT: plays come in numbered acts, here Act IV.
explanation.definitionFit: An activity is an undertaking or pursuit, the same as a project in the sense of something one is busy with.

clue.text: Understand tenor's committed to one night in Paris

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to be committed to a place is to be confined in it, so one letter goes inside the word

parts.note: nuit is French for night
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: A tenor commits to a single night's performance in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: T goes inside NUIT, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit is to know or grasp something by instinct, a sense of understanding without reasoning.

clue.text: Perhaps something Methuselah said scanned

wordplay.note: Methuselah, the Bible's longest-lived man at 969 years, might well declare his great age, split two and four

explanation.surface: A question about what the setter Methuselah, also the biblical patriarch, might have said.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is also this puzzle's setter, making it a wry self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Imaged describes a body part captured by a medical scan, so scanned and imaged mean the same.

clue.text: Partner after divorce papers, say?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
the press means newspapers

explanation.surface: Someone asks if the ex-spouse comes after the divorce papers are signed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' attached to papers; it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, so express is a verb synonym of say.

clue.text: Wrestler's a little too muscular to be flipped over

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it round, so the portion is read backwards
a little of the phrase means just a small portion sitting inside it

parts.note: the letters running across the two words, after the T and O

explanation.surface: A wrestler is a bit too brawny to be thrown on his back.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is Japanese heavyweight wrestling, and the word is also used for one of its wrestlers.

clue.text: Has more than ridiculous amounts

indicators.note: something ridiculous is absurd and out of order, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone owns far more of something than anyone could need.
explanation.definitionFit: To outman is to outnumber in people, so a side that outmans another has more players than it.

clue.text: Leads from random encounter could change entire investigation

indicators.note: leads are the front runners, so each word gives its opening letter

parts.note: the first letters of these five words

explanation.surface: Clues from a chance meeting could transform a whole police inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' sounds like detective clues in the surface; it means the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce, short for reconnaissance, is a scouting survey to find things out, a military or informal inquiry.

clue.text: Tackle with great speed finishes off uneven game for City

parts.note: Mach 1 is the speed of sound, written MACH I

indicators.note: the finishes of words are their final letters, taken from each word in turn

parts.note: the final letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A footballer tackles at pace as City's lopsided match comes to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tackle' wants to be a football challenge; it is the noun for equipment. City is a football club nickname, as Manchester City.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle as a noun means gear or apparatus, such as lifting equipment, which is machinery.
